global_issues.title: Middle East Strikes Send Oil to $90, Yields to Multi-Decade Highs
global_issues.note: WTI confirmed at ~$90.67 on 2026-09-01 (up 5.7%), driven by renewed US-Iran strikes near the Strait of Hormuz. However, '10-year yields to multi-decade highs' overstates it — reporting (CNBC, Forbes) describes the 10-year at ~4.80%, the highest since January 2025 (a ~19-month high), not a multi-decade high. Directionally correct but the magnitude is exaggerated.

global_issues.title: Trump Weighs New Chip Tariffs on Servers and Laptops
global_issues.note: Confirmed still developing as of Sept 1: Politico/CNBC reported (Aug 27) the administration is weighing extending the 25% chip tariff to laptops, servers, and consoles, potentially scrapping January's data-center exemptions. No final decision has been announced, consistent with 'developing' status.

market_mood_check.note: Yellow/75.6 with a headline emphasizing oil spike and NVDA pressure is directionally reasonable given the Iran/Hormuz and tariff overhang, but actual Sept 1 market action shows broad index declines (Dow -0.7%, S&P -0.3%) plus a global bond selloff explicitly described in press coverage — this systemic bond-selloff framing is understated relative to source reporting.

sector_check.note: CEG is framed as a beneficiary of the 'oil spike narrative' but CEG is a nuclear/utility company whose relative strength is driven primarily by AI power-demand growth, not oil prices — the causal link to the oil spike is weak/misleading. TSLA/GOOGL/PLTR downtrend framing is broadly consistent with reported tech softness.

stock_errors.error: Mood tagged 'optimistic' despite contemporaneous reporting that MU fell ~2% premarket specifically due to chip-tariff uncertainty — same tariff risk the briefing itself flags as global issue #2

Sector analysis attributes CEG's relative strength to the 'oil spike narrative,' but CEG is a nuclear/clean-energy utility with no meaningful direct exposure to oil prices; its strength is more plausibly tied to AI/data-center power demand

grok_report.summary: The two headline global issues (Iran/Hormuz oil spike, chip tariff threat) are both accurate and current, though the '10-year yields to multi-decade highs' claim overstates reality (actual: ~19-month/Jan-2025 high). The briefing understates the magnitude of the broad Sept 1 equity selloff and mislabels MU's mood as optimistic despite tariff-driven premarket weakness it itself flagged. The CEG-oil linkage in the sector analysis is a weak causal claim.
